title: Feijoada
subtitle: Brazilian black bean and pork stew
excerpt: Black beans slow-cooked with smoked pork sausage, pork ribs, and bacon until the beans are creamy and the broth is deeply savoury and rich. Brazil's national dish, served with rice, farofa, and orange slices.

recipe.sourceNotes: Feijoada is the national dish of Brazil and is found in some form across all Brazilian-speaking countries, including Portugal (where it uses white beans) and Mozambique. The Brazilian version uses black beans and the various cuts of pork that were traditionally available to enslaved Africans on Brazilian plantations: the tougher, fattier, and less desirable cuts. The stew is eaten on Saturdays in restaurants and homes across Brazil, a tradition linked to the long cooking time required. The full traditional version uses ears, tail, snout, and trotters; the simplified version uses more accessible cuts while maintaining the same bean and broth character.

recipeTools.notes: Large, heavy casserole for the long stew.

content.text: Soak the black beans overnight in plenty of cold water: this reduces the cooking time significantly. The bean soaking water should be discarded: it contains compounds that cause digestive discomfort. The stew needs the full time to develop its flavour and to let the beans become creamy rather than firm. Skim the fat from the surface as it cooks if you want a cleaner result, though some fat in the finished stew is traditional and adds richness.

Heat the oil in a large heavy casserole. Brown the pork ribs in batches over high heat. Remove and set aside. Fry the lardons and sausage for 3 minutes until lightly coloured. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the drained black beans and return the ribs to the pot. Cover with cold water by about 5 cm. Add the bay leaves. Bring to a boil, skim any foam, then reduce to a low simmer. Cook, partially covered, for 2.5 to 3 hours until the beans are completely soft and creamy and the broth has thickened and darkened. Add more water during cooking if the level drops too low.
Season with salt and pepper. Remove the bay leaves. Serve in deep bowls with steamed rice, sliced orange on the side, and hot sauce.
